def asks(body):
    """The kinds of ask in a supplier e-mail, in a fixed order. The bots write their asks in a few
    fixed sentences ("Which volume can you commit to?", "Please send us the data."), so plain
    patterns read them; no model, no latency."""
    text = body or ""
    return [k for k, pat in ASKS.items() if re.search(pat, text, re.I)]


class Side:
    """One supplier thread: what we know and what we did."""

    def __init__(self, sid):
        self.sid = sid
        self.std = {}
        self.prof = {}
        self.est = {}
        self.terms = {}  # our planned non-price terms (with a price placeholder)
        self.quote = None  # its opening price at our terms
        self.last_sheet = {}  # its previous standing terms
        self.late = 0  # our messages the arena counted as rounds although they came too late
        self.anchor = None
        self.target = None  # relationship goals: the price with the lowest C
        self.budget = BUDGET
        self.claims = []
        self.ours = []  # our prices at s.terms, one per message with a sheet
        self.theirs = []  # its price at our terms, one per reply
        self.gaps = []  # relative gap of each of our sheets to its counter
        self.state = "open"  # open | mirror | closing | done | ended
        self.prev_state = "open"  # the state before the message in flight
        self.pending = None  # the message in flight: what to undo if it times out
        self.last_sent_terms = None  # last committed primary sheet, for the no-progress guard
        self.used_claim_families = set()  # semantic evidence already used with this supplier
        self.offered_trade_keys = set()  # term/value alternatives already offered in this thread
        self.term_change = False  # its last counter changed our non-price terms
        self.last_reply = None
        self.asks = []  # what its last e-mail asked of us (asks)
        self.attached = set()  # files we already sent it
        self.research = ""  # the lead researcher's notes for the e-mail writer
        self.trades = []  # terms the lead expects it to value: offered next to our opening sheet
        self.active_trades = []  # explicit supplier needs priced for the current move
        self.playbook = {}  # the demo bidding: its expected arguments, our answers, points to press
        self.live = ""  # the live analyst's notes on its last e-mail
        self.mood = None  # the live analyst on its last e-mail: the writer's mood
        self.tactic = None  # and our next move: steady | hold | close_in | argue
        self.tactics = []  # every tactic played, for the debrief
        self.argument = 0  # which expected argument its last e-mail made (1-based), 0 for none


class Negotiator:
    def __init__(self, case, pkg=None, complete=None, briefs=None):
        """`briefs`: the research team's brief per supplier (`research.briefs`); None plays the
        plain price engine, without the research strategy and without the live analyst."""
        self.case, self.pkg, self.complete, self.briefs = case, pkg, complete, briefs
        self.bank = ClaimBank(pkg, case)
        self.sides = {}
        self.used = set()  # claim IDs cited in this case (a rival quote: per supplier)
        self.notes = []  # what we decided, for the log
        self.writer_s = llm.TIMEOUT_S  # wall clock the model may take on the move being built

    # -- setup -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def setup(self, sid, events):
        case, s = self.case, Side(sid)
        s.std = safe(lambda: standard_terms(events), {}) or {}
        sheet_id, quote = standing(events)
        s.prof = safe(lambda: profile(self.pkg, sid), profile(None, sid))
        self.read_signals(s, latest(events).get("body"))
        brief = (self.briefs or {}).get(sid) or {}
        self.sides[sid] = s
        if not sheet_id or quote.get("unit_price") is None:
            s.state = "ended"
            return s
        s.last_sheet = quote
        # a bundle's should-cost is unknown: one component's cost is not the price unit of the kit
        parts = case.get("parts") or []
        full_cost, own_plant = (
            safe(lambda: self.full_cost(parts[0], sid), (None, False)) if len(parts) == 1 else (None, False)
        )
        lead = quote.get("lead_time_days") or s.std.get("lead_time_days")
        overtime = 0.005 if "capacity_full" in s.prof["signals"] else 0.001
        s.est = eco.estimate(
            case, s.std or quote, s.prof["rate"], full_cost, safe(lambda: self.real_ppm(sid)), lead, overtime
        )
        q_price = quote["unit_price"]
        goal, signals = case["buyer"].get("category_goal"), s.prof["signals"]
        sustainable = case["buyer"].get("sustainable_margin_pct") or 0
        if full_cost and goal in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
            # it quoted with its margin: a should-cost above that is our estimate's error (P02: 374.95
            # against a quote of 370.96; the relationship charge of the deals says about 368)
            full_cost = min(full_cost, eco.value(case, quote, s.est) * (1 - sustainable / 100))
            s.est["full_cost"] = full_cost
        ratio = ANCHOR.get(goal, 0.85)
        near_cost = bool(own_plant and full_cost >= 0.98 * q_price)  # it sells at our cost estimate
        if goal in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
            s.budget = 0.3
        if "price_frozen" in signals:
            ratio = max(ratio, 0.95)  # its list price does not move far; a deep cut only costs patience
        if "capacity_full" in signals:
            ratio, s.budget = max(ratio, 0.93), min(s.budget, 0.16)
        if near_cost:
            ratio, s.budget = max(ratio, 0.97), min(s.budget, 0.14)
        current = case["buyer"].get("current_unit_price")
        if case.get("type") == "price_increase" and current:
            ratio = min(ratio, current / q_price)  # a price increase opens at today's price at most
        ratio = max(ANCHOR_MIN, ratio)
        if brief:
            self.apply(s, brief)
        # terms planned at the price we open with: coverage pays off at a low price, not at the quote
        planned = safe(lambda: eco.plan_terms(case, s.std, s.est, quote, q_price * ratio))
        s.terms = planned[0] if planned else eco.complete_offer(case, eco.at_price(quote, q_price * ratio))
        s.anchor = s.terms["unit_price"]
        s.quote = safe(
            lambda: round(eco.price_for_value(case, s.terms, s.est, eco.value(case, quote, s.est)), 2), q_price
        )
        if full_cost:
            # also for a supplier selling at our cost estimate: below the optimum a lower price costs
            # us more than it saves, and pushing on made Nordmark withdraw (P02 v1)
            s.target = safe(lambda: eco.relationship_optimum(case, s.terms, s.std, s.est, full_cost * 0.85, s.quote))
        safe(lambda: self.trade_clause(s, quote, full_cost))
        s.claims = safe(lambda: self.bank.for_supplier(sid, q_price), [])
        order = brief.get("claim_order") or []  # the arguments the lead expects this supplier to accept, first
        s.claims.sort(key=lambda c: order.index(c["kind"]) if c["kind"] in order else len(order))
        self.note(
            sid,
            "setup",
            quote=quote,
            std=s.std,
            profile=s.prof,
            full_cost=full_cost,
            near_cost=near_cost,
            terms=s.terms,
            quote_at_terms=s.quote,
            anchor=s.anchor,
            target=s.target,
            budget=s.budget,
            claims=[c["text"] for c in s.claims],
        )
        return s

    def apply(self, s, brief):
        """The research team's brief on this thread: the lead's trades wait for our opening sheet,
        the demo bidding's playbook for the supplier's arguments; notes and tone go to the e-mail
        writer. Prices and pace stay with the policy: a model moving them cost score (D01, D02,
        P04, `docs/learnings.md`)."""
        s.research = brief.get("notes") or ""
        s.trades = brief.get("trades") or []
        s.playbook = brief.get("playbook") or {}
        if brief.get("tone"):
            s.prof["warm"] = brief["tone"] == "warm"
        self.note(
            s.sid,
            "research",
            trades=s.trades,
            reason=brief.get("reason"),
            playbook=s.playbook,
            findings=brief.get("findings"),
        )

    def trade_sheets(self, s, main):
        """The lead's trades as extra sheets next to our opening sheet `main`: each changes one
        term and carries the price at which it costs us exactly what `main` costs, so whichever
        the supplier picks, we lose nothing and learn what it values. A trade whose price would
        sit at or above what the supplier quotes for those terms, or far below it, is not offered."""
        case, out = self.case, []
        c_main = eco.cost(case, main, s.std, s.est)
        for trade in s.trades:
            terms = {**main, trade["field"]: trade["value"]}
            if terms == main or not eco.must_haves_ok(case, terms, s.std):
                continue
            lo, hi = 0.0, main["unit_price"] * 3
            if (
                not eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(terms, lo), s.std, s.est)
                < c_main
                < eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(terms, hi), s.std, s.est)
            ):
                continue
            for _ in range(50):  # C rises with the price
                mid = (lo + hi) / 2
                lo, hi = (mid, hi) if eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(terms, mid), s.std, s.est) < c_main else (lo, mid)
            sheet = eco.at_price(terms, int(lo * 100) / 100)
            quoted = eco.price_for_value(case, terms, s.est, eco.value(case, eco.at_price(s.terms, s.quote), s.est))
            if not TRADE_MIN * quoted <= sheet["unit_price"] < 0.995 * quoted:
                continue
            out.append(sheet)
            self.note(s.sid, "trade_sheet", trade=trade, price=sheet["unit_price"], quoted=round(quoted, 2))
        return out

    def trade_clause(self, s, quote, full_cost):
        """An index clause the supplier values more than it costs us (its driver rose over the
        year, the case's path is small): offer it from the start at the price worth the same to it
        as our anchor without it, and in a relationship goal no lower than the relationship
        optimum, where it is agreed at once (P02: Nordmark agreed to a 5 % copper deadband 4 %
        below its fixed price). No trade where its value equals our cost (P08, P18)."""
        case = self.case
        if "index_clause" not in case["negotiable"] or quote.get("index_clause"):
            return
        if "hedged" in s.prof["signals"]:
            return  # its material is bought forward at fixed prices: the index does not reach its costs
        for clause in case.get("term_options", {}).get("index_clause") or []:
            if clause and clause.get("series") not in s.est["index_moves"]:
                move = self.bank.move12(clause["series"])
                if move is not None:
                    s.est["index_moves"][clause["series"]] = move
        clause = eco.clause_trade(case, s.est)
        if not clause or s.terms.get("index_clause") == clause:
            return
        target_value = eco.value(case, s.terms, s.est)  # our anchor as it is worth to the supplier
        terms = {**s.terms, "index_clause": clause}
        price = eco.price_for_value(case, terms, s.est, target_value)
        floor = None
        if full_cost and case["buyer"].get("category_goal") in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
            floor = eco.relationship_optimum(case, terms, s.std, s.est, full_cost * 0.85, s.quote)
            price = max(price, floor or 0.0)
        if not eco.must_haves_ok(case, eco.at_price(terms, price), s.std):
            return
        s.terms = eco.at_price(terms, price)
        s.anchor = s.terms["unit_price"]
        s.target = floor or s.target
        self.note(s.sid, "clause_trade", clause=clause, anchor=s.anchor, target=s.target)

    def full_cost(self, part, sid):
        """(should-cost of the part, whether it models this supplier's own plant): full cost
        without margin. A generic estimate (a German cost base) says little about one supplier."""
        rows = self.bank.query("SELECT id, supplier_id, unit_cost FROM should_cost WHERE part_id = ?", (part,))
        own = [r for r in rows if r.get("supplier_id") == sid]
        if own:
            return own[0]["unit_cost"], True
        generic = [r for r in rows if not r.get("supplier_id")]
        if generic:
            return generic[0]["unit_cost"], False
        for ref in self.bank.ids("cost:"):  # the case's own facts (no table rows)
            f = self.bank.fact(ref)
            if f and f.get("part") == part and f.get("unit_cost"):
                return f["unit_cost"], f.get("supplier") == sid
        return None, False

    def real_ppm(self, sid):
        """The defect rate it really delivers (latest scorecard), what a chargeback costs it."""
        ids = self.bank.ids(f"sc:{sid.split(':')[-1]}@")
        f = self.bank.fact(ids[-1]) if ids else None
        return f.get("ppm") if f else None

    def restore(self, sid, events):
        """A resumed session (a crash, a restart): rebuild what we sent and what it answered from
        the thread, so the next move continues the path instead of opening at the anchor again."""
        s = self.sides[sid]
        ours = [m for m in events if m.get("from") == "buyer" and m.get("term_sheets")]
        if s.state == "ended" or not ours:
            return
        s.terms = eco.complete_offer(self.case, ours[-1]["term_sheets"][0]["terms"])
        theirs = None
        for m in events:
            if m.get("from") == "buyer":
                refs = m.get("refs") or []
                self.used.update(refs)
                s.used_claim_families.update(
                    family for ref in refs for family in self.claim_families({"kind": "forecast", "ids": [ref]})
                )
                if m.get("term_sheets"):
                    sent_sheets = [sh.get("terms") or {} for sh in m["term_sheets"]]
                    s.last_sent_terms = dict(sent_sheets[0])
                    s.offered_trade_keys.update(self.trade_keys(sent_sheets))
                    price = self.their_price(s, m["term_sheets"][0]["terms"])
                    s.ours.append(price)
                    s.gaps.append(max(0.0, (theirs - price) / theirs) if theirs else 0.0)
            else:
                sheets = m.get("term_sheets") or []
                if sheets and sheets[0].get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") is not None:
                    theirs = self.their_price(s, sheets[0]["terms"])
                    if s.ours:
                        s.theirs.append(theirs)
        if events and events[-1].get("from") != "buyer" and s.theirs:
            s.theirs.pop()  # the latest reply is read by move() like any fresh reply
        self.note(sid, "restore", ours=s.ours, theirs=s.theirs, terms=s.terms)

    # -- reading its reply -------------------------------------------------------------------
    def read_signals(self, s, body):
        """Persona traits in its own e-mail (a supplier the package does not know, or news since):
        merged into the profile; a cash need raises what money now is worth to it."""
        new = [k for k in signals_in(body) if k not in s.prof["signals"]]
        if not new:
            return
        s.prof["signals"] = sorted(s.prof["signals"] + new)
        if "cash_need" in new:
            s.prof["rate"] = round(s.prof["rate"] + 0.05, 3)
            if s.est:
                s.est["interest_rate"] = s.prof["rate"]
        self.note(s.sid, "signals", new=new)

    def listen(self, s, body):
        """The live analyst on its latest e-mail: the mood goes to the writer, the tactic paces our
        next price and our evidence, the argument it recognised picks our prepared answer, its
        asks join what the patterns found. Its time comes out of the writer's; late or off, the
        move goes on with the patterns alone."""
        s.mood, s.tactic, s.argument = None, None, 0
        if self.writer_s < ANALYST_MIN_S:  # several threads share the clocks: the move comes first
            return
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        arguments = s.playbook.get("arguments") or []
        seen = analyst.read(self.complete, self.case, body, s.ours, s.theirs, arguments, self.writer_s / 2)
        self.writer_s -= time.monotonic() - t0
        if seen is None:
            return
        s.asks = [k for k in ASKS if k in s.asks or k in seen["asks"]]
        s.mood, s.tactic, s.argument, s.live = seen["mood"], seen["tactic"], seen["argument"], seen["notes"]
        s.tactics.append(s.tactic)
        self.note(s.sid, "analyst", seconds=round(time.monotonic() - t0, 1), **seen)

    def team_facts(self, s, first, extra):
        """What the team adds to the writer's facts: our prepared answer to the argument its e-mail
        made, a weak point to press in the opening, the trades on offer, the mood to meet."""
        out = []
        rebuttals = s.playbook.get("rebuttals") or []
        if s.argument and s.argument <= len(rebuttals) and rebuttals[s.argument - 1]:
            out.append(
                f'they argue: "{s.playbook["arguments"][s.argument - 1]}" Our answer, in your own words: '
                f"{rebuttals[s.argument - 1]}"
            )
        if first and s.playbook.get("press"):
            out.append(f"a point to raise politely, once: {s.playbook['press'][0]}")
        if extra:
            why = "; ".join(t["why"] for t in [*s.trades, *s.active_trades] if t.get("why"))
            out.append(
                "our proposal lists alternative packages after the first one: say they are free to choose the "
                f"one that suits them best ({why})"
            )
        elif s.active_trades:
            why = "; ".join(t["why"] for t in s.active_trades if t.get("why"))
            out.append(f"we adjusted the package in response to {why}; explain the commercial terms clearly")
        if s.mood == "irritated":
            out.append("they sound irritated: acknowledge it sincerely before anything else")
        elif s.mood == "pressured":
            out.append("they sound under pressure: be calm and make the next step easy for them")
        return out

    def their_price(self, s, terms):
        """Its sheet as a price at our planned terms (same value to it)."""
        same = all(terms.get(k) == v for k, v in s.terms.items() if k != "unit_price" and k in terms)
        if same:
            return terms["unit_price"]
        v = eco.value(self.case, terms, s.est)
        return round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, s.terms, s.est, v), 2)

    def switch(self, s, new, why):
        """Plan new non-price terms; our last price moves to the same value for the supplier."""
        if s.ours:
            v = eco.value(self.case, eco.at_price(s.terms, s.ours[-1]), s.est)
            s.ours[-1] = round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, new, s.est, v), 2)
        if s.theirs:
            v = eco.value(self.case, eco.at_price(s.terms, s.theirs[-1]), s.est)
            s.theirs[-1] = round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, new, s.est, v), 2)
        s.terms = {**new}
        self.note(s.sid, "switch_terms", why=why, terms={k: v for k, v in new.items() if k != "unit_price"})

    def adopt(self, s, sheets):
        """Compare complete quoted packages, then switch once to the cheapest useful one."""
        if not s.ours:
            return
        case = self.case
        standing = sheets[0]["terms"]
        planned_cost = eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(s.terms, self.their_price(s, standing)), s.std, s.est)
        candidates = []
        for sheet in sheets:
            new = eco.quoted_offer(case, sheet["terms"], s.std)
            if new is None or all(new.get(k) == v for k, v in s.terms.items() if k != "unit_price"):
                continue
            c = eco.deal_cost(case, new, s.std, s.est)
            if c is not None and c < planned_cost - max(1.0, 0.001 * planned_cost):
                candidates.append((c, new))
        if candidates:
            _, new = min(candidates, key=lambda row: (row[0], repr(sorted(row[1].items()))))
            self.switch(s, new, "complete quoted package costs us less")

    # -- one move ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def move(self, sid, threads, writer_s=llm.TIMEOUT_S):
        """The next message to this supplier: {"message": ...}, or None when the thread is done.
        `writer_s`: what the supplier clocks leave for the model paragraph."""
        s, events = self.sides[sid], threads[sid]
        self.writer_s = writer_s
        s.prev_state = s.state
        last = latest(events)
        status = last.get("status")
        if s.state == "ended" or status in ENDED:
            s.state = "ended"
            return None
        sheets = [sh for sh in last.get("term_sheets") or [] if sh.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") is not None]
        if not sheets:
            s.state = "ended" if not standing(events)[0] else "done"
            return None
        std_before = s.std
        s.std = standard_terms(events) or s.std
        fresh = s.last_reply is not last
        if fresh:
            terms_before = dict(s.terms)
            estimate_before = dict(s.est)
            self.adopt(s, sheets)
            s.term_change = any(sheets[0]["terms"].get(k, v) != v for k, v in terms_before.items() if k != "unit_price")
            s.theirs.append(self.their_price(s, sheets[0]["terms"]))
            s.last_sheet = sheets[0]["terms"]
            s.last_reply = last
            s.asks = asks(last.get("body"))
            self.read_signals(s, last.get("body"))
            if self.briefs is not None and status not in DONE:
                self.listen(s, last.get("body"))
            economics_changed = s.terms != terms_before or s.est != estimate_before or s.std != std_before
            if s.target is not None and economics_changed:
                s.target = eco.relationship_optimum(
                    self.case,
                    s.terms,
                    s.std,
                    s.est,
                    s.est["full_cost"] * 0.85,
                    max(s.est["full_cost"] * 0.85, s.quote, s.target, s.theirs[-1]),
                )
        theirs = s.theirs[-1]
        if s.state in ("mirror", "closing"):  # we sent its own sheet or our target: done
            s.state = "done"
            return None
        left = self.moves_left(s, events)
        if status in DONE or left <= 0:
            return self.finish(s, sheets, events, theirs, left)
        if s.ours and s.target and theirs <= s.target:
            # relationship goal: below the target a lower price costs more than it saves
            s.state = "closing"
            sheet = eco.at_price(s.terms, max(s.target, theirs))
            if self.same_offer(s.last_sent_terms, sheet):
                s.state = "done"
                self.note(sid, "no_progress", reason="relationship target already offered")
                return None
            return self.send(s, [sheet], [], events, theirs)
        if s.ours and theirs <= s.ours[-1]:  # it came below what we offered: take it
            return self.finish(s, sheets, events, theirs, left)
        price, n_claims = self.next_price(s, theirs)
        claims = self.pick(s, n_claims, threads)
        sheets = [eco.at_price(s.terms, price)]
        if not s.ours and s.trades:
            sheets += safe(lambda: self.trade_sheets(s, sheets[0]), [])[:2]
        elif s.ours:
            sheets += safe(lambda: self.need_trade_sheets(s, sheets[0]), [])[:2]
        switched_trade_keys = set()
        if self.same_offer(s.last_sent_terms, sheets[0]):
            if len(sheets) == 1:
                s.state = "done"
                self.note(sid, "no_progress", reason="unchanged price and terms")
                return None
            # Do not resend the old primary sheet. Move the thread onto the best new package,
            # whose buyer cost is lower and whose estimated supplier value matches the main offer.
            switched_trade_keys = self.trade_keys(sheets)
            sheet = sheets[1]
            old_target = s.target
            self.switch(s, sheet, "cost-checked response to a supplier need")
            if old_target is not None and s.est.get("full_cost"):
                floor = s.est["full_cost"] * 0.85
                s.target = eco.relationship_optimum(
                    self.case,
                    s.terms,
                    s.std,
                    s.est,
                    floor,
                    max(floor, s.quote, old_target, s.theirs[-1]),
                )
            sheets = [sheet]
        result = self.send(s, sheets, claims, events, theirs)
        if s.pending and switched_trade_keys:
            s.pending["trade_keys"].update(switched_trade_keys)
        return result

    def moves_left(self, s, events):
        """Messages we may still send: the arena counts a late message as a round too."""
        return moves_left(self.case, events) - s.late

    def next_price(self, s, theirs):
        """Our next price at s.terms: open at the anchor; then a share of the gap, held low after a
        large concession, and within the patience budget."""
        if not s.ours:
            return s.anchor, FIRST_CLAIMS
        last = s.ours[-1]
        conceded = (s.theirs[-2] - theirs) / s.theirs[-2] if len(s.theirs) > 1 else 0.0
        fraction = FRACTION * (HOLD if s.tactic == "hold" else 1.0)

        return round(max(price, last), 2), LATER_CLAIMS + (s.tactic == "argue")  # an argument gets evidence

    def finish(self, s, sheets, events, theirs, left):

"""The negotiation policy, per supplier thread: plan the non-price terms by C at the supplier's
own valuation, open below its quote, then move toward its counter round by round so it keeps
conceding, with verified claims spread over the rounds. Close on its final offer, its agreement or
the round limit; in relationship goals stop at the price where C is lowest.

What the suppliers showed (sandbox and practice, `docs/learnings.md`):
- they concede only after a move from us and agree as soon as our sheet reaches the counter they
  would make, so our sheet stays below their counter until the end;
- every verified claim they take into account lowers where they stop, most of it in round 1;
- patience runs out at a cumulative gap of about 40 % between our sheets and their counters
  (summed per round, relative to their price), much earlier for a supplier selling near its cost
  or one that is fully booked: a final offer, or a walk-away;
- a large first concession means a deep floor: then we hold low instead of meeting it."""

import base64
import functools
import json
import logging
import re
import time

from arena_kit.docs import standard_terms
from arena_kit.play import ENDED, latest, live_threads, moves_left, standing

from . import analyst, llm, writer
from . import economics as eco
from .claims import ClaimBank, rival_offer
from .personas import profile, signals_in

log = logging.getLogger("buyer")

FRACTION = 0.3  # share of the gap to the supplier's counter we move per round
# Opening price as a share of its quote at our terms, by category goal. Practice C_best sat 12 to
# 22 % below the quote in leverage, routine and secure-supply cases, 1.5 to 3 % in stabilise ones.
ANCHOR = {"leverage": 0.78, "routine": 0.82, "secure_supply": 0.88, "quality_first": 0.88, "stabilise": 0.92}
ANCHOR_MIN = 0.75  # never open lower than this share (an insult costs patience)
BUDGET = 1.0  # patience: the cumulative relative gap we show (no cap for a typical supplier)
DEEP = 0.06  # a first concession this large (share of its quote) means a deep floor
MIN_MOVE = 0.002  # every sheet moves at least this share of the price
FIRST_CLAIMS, LATER_CLAIMS = 3, 1
HOLD = 0.7  # the live analyst's "hold": it still concedes, we move this share of our usual step
CLOSE_IN = 0.5  # "close_in": the end is near, we close this share of the gap (never a jump to its price)
ANALYST_MIN_S = 10.0  # the clocks must leave this much for analyst and writer together, else no analyst
TRADE_MIN = 0.7  # a trade sheet's price never sits below this share of what the supplier quotes for it
DONE = {"agreed", "final_offer"}

# What the supplier's e-mail asks of us
ASKS = {
    # a binding volume figure; stated in words with the figure, it was "taken into account" (D01, D02)
    "volume": r"volume (can )?you (can )?commit|binding (higher )?volume|higher (order )?volume|volume figures"
    r"|confirm .{0,40}volume|anticipated (order )?volume",
    # proof of the forecast or of figures we mentioned without an ID
    "proof": r"proof of|send us the data|figures is that based|provide the (volume|forecast|binding)"
    r"|forecast data|volume data",
    # it wants to be paid sooner
    "payment": r"faster payment|pay(ment)? (terms )?(earlier|faster|sooner|within)|need .{0,12}days payment"
    r"|shorter payment|quicker payment|cash flow",
    # it asks for our current price level or our target
    "target": r"what price|which price|your target|price you have in mind",
}


def asks(body):
    """The kinds of ask in a supplier e-mail, in a fixed order. The bots write their asks in a few
    fixed sentences ("Which volume can you commit to?", "Please send us the data."), so plain
    patterns read them; no model, no latency."""
    text = body or ""
    return [k for k, pat in ASKS.items() if re.search(pat, text, re.I)]


class Side:
    """One supplier thread: what we know and what we did."""

    def __init__(self, sid):
        self.sid = sid
        self.std = {}
        self.prof = {}
        self.est = {}
        self.terms = {}  # our planned non-price terms (with a price placeholder)
        self.quote = None  # its opening price at our terms
        self.last_sheet = {}  # its previous standing terms
        self.late = 0  # our messages the arena counted as rounds although they came too late
        self.anchor = None
        self.target = None  # relationship goals: the price with the lowest C
        self.budget = BUDGET
        self.claims = []
        self.ours = []  # our prices at s.terms, one per message with a sheet
        self.theirs = []  # its price at our terms, one per reply
        self.gaps = []  # relative gap of each of our sheets to its counter
        self.state = "open"  # open | mirror | closing | done | ended
        self.prev_state = "open"  # the state before the message in flight
        self.pending = None  # the message in flight: what to undo if it times out
        self.last_sent_terms = None  # last committed primary sheet, for the no-progress guard
        self.used_claim_families = set()  # semantic evidence already used with this supplier
        self.offered_trade_keys = set()  # term/value alternatives already offered in this thread
        self.term_change = False  # its last counter changed our non-price terms
        self.last_reply = None
        self.asks = []  # what its last e-mail asked of us (asks)
        self.attached = set()  # files we already sent it
        self.research = ""  # the lead researcher's notes for the e-mail writer
        self.trades = []  # terms the lead expects it to value: offered next to our opening sheet
        self.active_trades = []  # explicit supplier needs priced for the current move
        self.playbook = {}  # the demo bidding: its expected arguments, our answers, points to press
        self.live = ""  # the live analyst's notes on its last e-mail
        self.mood = None  # the live analyst on its last e-mail: the writer's mood
        self.tactic = None  # and our next move: steady | hold | close_in | argue
        self.tactics = []  # every tactic played, for the debrief
        self.argument = 0  # which expected argument its last e-mail made (1-based), 0 for none


class Negotiator:
    def __init__(self, case, pkg=None, complete=None, briefs=None):
        """`briefs`: the research team's brief per supplier (`research.briefs`); None plays the
        plain price engine, without the research strategy and without the live analyst."""
        self.case, self.pkg, self.complete, self.briefs = case, pkg, complete, briefs
        self.bank = ClaimBank(pkg, case)
        self.sides = {}
        self.used = set()  # claim IDs cited in this case (a rival quote: per supplier)
        self.notes = []  # what we decided, for the log
        self.writer_s = llm.TIMEOUT_S  # wall clock the model may take on the move being built

    # -- setup -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def setup(self, sid, events):
        case, s = self.case, Side(sid)
        s.std = safe(lambda: standard_terms(events), {}) or {}
        sheet_id, quote = standing(events)
        s.prof = safe(lambda: profile(self.pkg, sid), profile(None, sid))
        self.read_signals(s, latest(events).get("body"))
        brief = (self.briefs or {}).get(sid) or {}
        self.sides[sid] = s
        if not sheet_id or quote.get("unit_price") is None:
            s.state = "ended"
            return s
        s.last_sheet = quote
        # a bundle's should-cost is unknown: one component's cost is not the price unit of the kit
        parts = case.get("parts") or []
        full_cost, own_plant = (
            safe(lambda: self.full_cost(parts[0], sid), (None, False)) if len(parts) == 1 else (None, False)
        )
        lead = quote.get("lead_time_days") or s.std.get("lead_time_days")
        overtime = 0.005 if "capacity_full" in s.prof["signals"] else 0.001
        s.est = eco.estimate(
            case, s.std or quote, s.prof["rate"], full_cost, safe(lambda: self.real_ppm(sid)), lead, overtime
        )
        q_price = quote["unit_price"]
        goal, signals = case["buyer"].get("category_goal"), s.prof["signals"]
        sustainable = case["buyer"].get("sustainable_margin_pct") or 0
        if full_cost and goal in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
            # it quoted with its margin: a should-cost above that is our estimate's error (P02: 374.95
            # against a quote of 370.96; the relationship charge of the deals says about 368)
            full_cost = min(full_cost, eco.value(case, quote, s.est) * (1 - sustainable / 100))
            s.est["full_cost"] = full_cost
        ratio = ANCHOR.get(goal, 0.85)
        near_cost = bool(own_plant and full_cost >= 0.98 * q_price)  # it sells at our cost estimate
        if goal in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
            s.budget = 0.3
        if "price_frozen" in signals:
            ratio = max(ratio, 0.95)  # its list price does not move far; a deep cut only costs patience
        if "capacity_full" in signals:
            ratio, s.budget = max(ratio, 0.93), min(s.budget, 0.16)
        if near_cost:
            ratio, s.budget = max(ratio, 0.97), min(s.budget, 0.14)
        current = case["buyer"].get("current_unit_price")
        if case.get("type") == "price_increase" and current:
            ratio = min(ratio, current / q_price)  # a price increase opens at today's price at most
        ratio = max(ANCHOR_MIN, ratio)
        if brief:
            self.apply(s, brief)
        # terms planned at the price we open with: coverage pays off at a low price, not at the quote
        planned = safe(lambda: eco.plan_terms(case, s.std, s.est, quote, q_price * ratio))
        s.terms = planned[0] if planned else eco.complete_offer(case, eco.at_price(quote, q_price * ratio))
        s.anchor = s.terms["unit_price"]
        s.quote = safe(
            lambda: round(eco.price_for_value(case, s.terms, s.est, eco.value(case, quote, s.est)), 2), q_price
        )
        if full_cost:
            # also for a supplier selling at our cost estimate: below the optimum a lower price costs
            # us more than it saves, and pushing on made Nordmark withdraw (P02 v1)
            s.target = safe(lambda: eco.relationship_optimum(case, s.terms, s.std, s.est, full_cost * 0.85, s.quote))
        safe(lambda: self.trade_clause(s, quote, full_cost))
        s.claims = safe(lambda: self.bank.for_supplier(sid, q_price), [])
        order = brief.get("claim_order") or []  # the arguments the lead expects this supplier to accept, first
        s.claims.sort(key=lambda c: order.index(c["kind"]) if c["kind"] in order else len(order))
        self.note(
            sid,
            "setup",
            quote=quote,
            std=s.std,
            profile=s.prof,
            full_cost=full_cost,
            near_cost=near_cost,
            terms=s.terms,
            quote_at_terms=s.quote,
            anchor=s.anchor,
            target=s.target,
            budget=s.budget,
            claims=[c["text"] for c in s.claims],
        )
        return s

    def apply(self, s, brief):
        """The research team's brief on this thread: the lead's trades wait for our opening sheet,
        the demo bidding's playbook for the supplier's arguments; notes and tone go to the e-mail
        writer. Prices and pace stay with the policy: a model moving them cost score (D01, D02,

"""The negotiation policy, per supplier thread: plan the non-price terms by C at the supplier's
own valuation, open below its quote, then move toward its counter round by round so it keeps
conceding, with verified claims spread over the rounds. Close on its final offer, its agreement or
the round limit; in relationship goals stop at the price where C is lowest.

- they concede only after a move from us and agree as soon as our sheet reaches the counter they
  would make, so our sheet stays below their counter until the end;
- every verified claim they take into account lowers where they stop, most of it in round 1;
- patience runs out at a cumulative gap of about 40 % between our sheets and their counters
  (summed per round, relative to their price), much earlier for a supplier selling near its cost
  or one that is fully booked: a final offer, or a walk-away;

    def full_cost(self, part, sid):
        """(should-cost of the part, whether it models this supplier's own plant): full cost
        without margin. A generic estimate (a German cost base) says little about one supplier."""
        rows = self.bank.query("SELECT id, supplier_id, unit_cost FROM should_cost WHERE part_id = ?", (part,))
        own = [r for r in rows if r.get("supplier_id") == sid]
        if own:
            return own[0]["unit_cost"], True
        generic = [r for r in rows if not r.get("supplier_id")]
        if generic:
            return generic[0]["unit_cost"], False
        for ref in self.bank.ids("cost:"):  # the case's own facts (no table rows)
            f = self.bank.fact(ref)
            if f and f.get("part") == part and f.get("unit_cost"):
                return f["unit_cost"], f.get("supplier") == sid
        return None, False

    def real_ppm(self, sid):
        """The defect rate it really delivers (latest scorecard), what a chargeback costs it."""
        ids = self.bank.ids(f"sc:{sid.split(':')[-1]}@")
        f = self.bank.fact(ids[-1]) if ids else None
        return f.get("ppm") if f else None

    def restore(self, sid, events):
        """A resumed session (a crash, a restart): rebuild what we sent and what it answered from
        the thread, so the next move continues the path instead of opening at the anchor again."""
        s = self.sides[sid]
        ours = [m for m in events if m.get("from") == "buyer" and m.get("term_sheets")]
        if s.state == "ended" or not ours:
            return
        s.terms = eco.complete_offer(self.case, ours[-1]["term_sheets"][0]["terms"])
        theirs = None
        for m in events:
            if m.get("from") == "buyer":
                refs = m.get("refs") or []
                self.used.update(refs)
                s.used_claim_families.update(
                    family for ref in refs for family in self.claim_families({"kind": "forecast", "ids": [ref]})
                )
                if m.get("term_sheets"):
                    sent_sheets = [sh.get("terms") or {} for sh in m["term_sheets"]]
                    s.last_sent_terms = dict(sent_sheets[0])
                    s.offered_trade_keys.update(self.trade_keys(sent_sheets))
                    price = self.their_price(s, m["term_sheets"][0]["terms"])
                    s.ours.append(price)
                    s.gaps.append(max(0.0, (theirs - price) / theirs) if theirs else 0.0)
            else:
                sheets = m.get("term_sheets") or []
                if sheets and sheets[0].get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") is not None:
                    theirs = self.their_price(s, sheets[0]["terms"])
                    if s.ours:
                        s.theirs.append(theirs)

    def read_signals(self, s, body):
        """Persona traits in its own e-mail (a supplier the package does not know, or news since):
        merged into the profile; a cash need raises what money now is worth to it."""
        new = [k for k in signals_in(body) if k not in s.prof["signals"]]
        if not new:
            return
        s.prof["signals"] = sorted(s.prof["signals"] + new)
        if "cash_need" in new:
            s.prof["rate"] = round(s.prof["rate"] + 0.05, 3)
            if s.est:
                s.est["interest_rate"] = s.prof["rate"]
        self.note(s.sid, "signals", new=new)

    def listen(self, s, body):
        """The live analyst on its latest e-mail: the mood goes to the writer, the tactic paces our
        next price and our evidence, the argument it recognised picks our prepared answer, its
        asks join what the patterns found. Its time comes out of the writer's; late or off, the
        move goes on with the patterns alone."""
        s.mood, s.tactic, s.argument = None, None, 0
        if self.writer_s < ANALYST_MIN_S:  # several threads share the clocks: the move comes first
            return
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        arguments = s.playbook.get("arguments") or []
        seen = analyst.read(self.complete, self.case, body, s.ours, s.theirs, arguments, self.writer_s / 2)
        self.writer_s -= time.monotonic() - t0
        if seen is None:
            return
        s.asks = [k for k in ASKS if k in s.asks or k in seen["asks"]]
        s.mood, s.tactic, s.argument, s.live = seen["mood"], seen["tactic"], seen["argument"], seen["notes"]
        s.tactics.append(s.tactic)
        self.note(s.sid, "analyst", seconds=round(time.monotonic() - t0, 1), **seen)

        """What the team adds to the writer's facts: our prepared answer to the argument its e-mail
        made, a weak point to press in the opening, the trades on offer, the mood to meet."""
        out = []
        rebuttals = s.playbook.get("rebuttals") or []
        if s.argument and s.argument <= len(rebuttals) and rebuttals[s.argument - 1]:
            out.append(
                f'they argue: "{s.playbook["arguments"][s.argument - 1]}" Our answer, in your own words: '
                f"{rebuttals[s.argument - 1]}"
            )
        if first and s.playbook.get("press"):
            out.append(f"a point to raise politely, once: {s.playbook['press'][0]}")
        if extra:
            why = "; ".join(t["why"] for t in [*s.trades, *s.active_trades] if t.get("why"))
            out.append(
                "our proposal lists alternative packages after the first one: say they are free to choose the "
                f"one that suits them best ({why})"
            )
        elif s.active_trades:
            why = "; ".join(t["why"] for t in s.active_trades if t.get("why"))
            out.append(f"we adjusted the package in response to {why}; explain the commercial terms clearly")
        if s.mood == "irritated":
            out.append("they sound irritated: acknowledge it sincerely before anything else")
        elif s.mood == "pressured":
            out.append("they sound under pressure: be calm and make the next step easy for them")
        return out

    def their_price(self, s, terms):
        """Its sheet as a price at our planned terms (same value to it)."""
        same = all(terms.get(k) == v for k, v in s.terms.items() if k != "unit_price" and k in terms)
        if same:
            return terms["unit_price"]
        v = eco.value(self.case, terms, s.est)
        return round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, s.terms, s.est, v), 2)

            s.ours[-1] = round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, new, s.est, v), 2)
        if s.theirs:
            v = eco.value(self.case, eco.at_price(s.terms, s.theirs[-1]), s.est)

# Exports: the Saturday probe sessions as tables

Every session we played on Saturday 10 October: 15 practice sessions (all 10 hosted cases) and 17
sandbox sessions, joined with the case files and the data package. What we learned from them is
in `docs/learnings.md`. Money is EUR over the case horizon; C is the arena's total cost
(`arena_kit.total_cost`), lower is better. This is a snapshot: the probe and the script that built
it (`buyer/autoprobe.py`, `analysis/export.py`) are in the closed PR #5, commit `03c51bc`.

| File | One row per | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `sessions.csv`, `.jsonl` | session | outcomes: score, C open/deal/alt/best, deal terms, cost breakdown |
| `threads.csv`, `.jsonl` | supplier in a session | supplier profile from the data next to what it did |
| `messages.jsonl` | e-mail, both directions | the full negotiation: terms with C, status, claims, reasons, back office |
| `claims.csv` | data argument we made | which arguments the arena verified, and for whom |

Join keys: `session_id` (+ `supplier_id`, + `round`). `set` is `practice` or `sandbox`.

## How we played

`method` in `sessions`:

- `autoprobe v1`: a fixed experiment per supplier thread, then the cheapest valid close. Its steps
  are `probe_step` in `messages` and `probe_steps` in `threads`:
  - `open`: questions and documents (cost breakdown, delivery schedule or 8D), our anchor price
  - `ours`: up to 3 sheets at the supplier's price, each with one lever moved our way
  - `theirs`: up to 3 sheets a step below, each with one lever moved its way
  - `claims`: up to 3 verified data arguments with a concession
  - `step`: concessions until `final_offer` or `agreed`; `push`: one ask after `agreed`
  - `keepalive`: a short question so a waiting RFQ thread does not time out

"""Numbers only: C of a sheet, what a sheet is worth to the supplier, the non-price terms we ask for
and, in relationship goals, the price below which a lower price costs us more than it saves.
Nothing here calls a model; every figure that reaches a term sheet comes from here."""

import itertools
import math

from arena_kit.cost import RELATIONSHIP_GOALS, closing_terms, complete_offer, must_haves_ok, supplier_value, total_cost


def cost(case, terms, std=None, est=None):
    """C in EUR; infinite for sheets the cost function cannot price. The relationship charge
    needs a full-cost estimate; without one it counts as 0."""
    if est is not None and not est.get("full_cost"):
        est = None
    try:
        return total_cost(case, terms, std, est)
    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, ZeroDivisionError):
        return math.inf


def c_alt(case):
    alt = case["buyer"].get("alternative") or {}
    terms = alt.get("terms") or {}
    if alt.get("kind") in (None, "none") or not terms.get("unit_price"):
        return math.inf
    return cost(case, terms)


def deal_cost(case, terms, std, est=None):
    """The accept gate: C of a sheet with a price that keeps every must-have and is cheaper than
    the alternative (relationship charge included), else None. The C returned is the C checked."""
    if not terms.get("unit_price") or not must_haves_ok(case, terms, std):
        return None
    c = cost(case, terms, std, est)
    return c if c < c_alt(case) else None


def quoted_offer(case, terms, std=None):
    """An outgoing sheet with exactly the quoted effective package, never snapped terms."""
    effective = closing_terms(case, terms, std)
    if any(effective.get(k) != v for k, v in case.get("fixed_terms", {}).items()):
        return None
    offer = {k: effective.get(k) for k in case["negotiable"]}
    price = offer.get("unit_price")
    if not isinstance(price, (int, float)) or not math.isfinite(price) or price <= 0:
        return None
    opts = case.get("term_options", {})
    if any(opts.get(k) and v not in opts[k] for k, v in offer.items()):
        return None
    if closing_terms(case, offer, std) != effective:
        return None
    return offer if must_haves_ok(case, offer, std) else None


def known_incoterm(case, terms):
    """`terms` with an Incoterm the case prices; an unknown one (a hidden case's quote) would be a
    KeyError in the kit, so it falls back to the costliest, as `closing_terms` does for a gap."""
    freight = case["buyer"]["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    if terms.get("incoterm") in freight or "incoterm" not in terms:
        return terms
    return {**terms, "incoterm": max(freight, key=freight.get)}


def estimate(case, std, rate, full_cost=None, ppm=None, lead=None, overtime=0.0):
    """Our view of the supplier for `supplier_value` and the relationship term. `lead`: the lead
    time it quoted; `overtime`: what each day faster costs it, as a share of the price."""
    standard = known_incoterm(case, closing_terms(case, {}, known_incoterm(case, std or {})))
    est = {"standard": standard, "interest_rate": rate, "lead": lead, "overtime": overtime}
    if ppm is not None:
        est["ppm"] = ppm
    if full_cost:
        est["full_cost"] = full_cost
    est["index_moves"] = {}  # series -> its change over the last 12 months (share), what the supplier expects on
    return est


# The most a supplier is assumed to value an index clause at, as a share of the price. The model
# below is linear in the driver's move and the material share; it is backed by one supplier that
# valued its clause at 8.5 % (Nordmark, P02). Copper's 48 % year would value a 55 % share at 24 %
# of the price (P14), which nothing supports.
CLAUSE_VALUE_MAX = 0.08


def clause_share(clause, est):
    """What a clause is worth to the supplier as a share of the price: it expects its driver to
    move on as it did over the last twelve months (what it cites in its quote), and the clause
    pays it that share beyond the deadband, capped at `CLAUSE_VALUE_MAX`. None without a move."""
    move = est.get("index_moves", {}).get(clause.get("series"))
    if move is None:
        return None
    exposed = max(0.0, move - (clause.get("deadband_pct") or 0) / 100)
    return min(CLAUSE_VALUE_MAX, (clause.get("material_share") or 0) * exposed)


def clause_value(terms, est):
    """What an index clause is worth to the supplier per unit. Nordmark agreed at once to a copper
    clause 4 % below its fixed price (P02); the distributors priced the AS-14404 deadband at
    exactly our cost (P08, P18)."""
    clause = terms.get("index_clause")
    if not clause:
        return 0.0
    share = clause_share(clause, est)
    return 0.0 if share is None else share * (terms.get("unit_price") or 0)


def clause_cost_share(case, clause):
    """Our cost of a clause as a share of the spend: the case's path beyond the deadband plus the
    index risk charge."""
    b = case["buyer"]
    share, deadband = clause.get("material_share") or 0, (clause.get("deadband_pct") or 0) / 100
    path = abs(b.get("index_paths", {}).get(clause.get("series"), 0.0))
    return share * max(0.0, path - deadband) + share * b.get("index_risk_pct", 0) / 100


def clause_trade(case, est, min_gain=0.02):
    """The index clause worth trading: the supplier's value less our cost, as a share of the price,
    above `min_gain`; among equal gains the widest deadband (least risk). None when no clause pays
    (P08, P18: the supplier's value equals our cost) or the case has none to offer."""

"""What the data says about a supplier before the first move: owner type, the persona traits in
its notes, letters, quote remarks and news (the package and the Sunday release alike), and from
those its cost of money. Unknown suppliers (not in the package, e.g. the sandbox) get the neutral
profile; their own e-mails are scanned for the same traits as they arrive (`signals_in`)."""

import re

# One or two fixed phrases per trait in the generated texts, widened to the word forms seen across
# the whole package (restructuring programme, lowered its rating, "nickel and alloys forward").
SIGNALS = {
    "cash_need": r"pay earlier|bank is watching|cash and the banks|within 10 days|under pressure"
    r"|restructur\w*|short-time work|lower\w* (its |their )?rating|cash is tight|we like fast payers"
    r"|negotiat\w+ with (its|their) banks|lowers our margin|loss-making|liquidity|waiting for cash",
    "spare_capacity": r"second shift has been on hold|take additional parts|looks for new customers"
    r"|free (machine )?capacity|keep (the|our) machines (busy|running)",
    "capacity_full": r"order intake is very strong|binding 12-month commitment"
    r"|cannot confirm your full forecast|fully booked|allocat\w+ (volumes|in line)|factory is super busy"
    r"|high capacity utili[sz]ation|prioriti[sz]e customers with firm",
    "open_book": r"walk (us|you) through (their|our) calculation",
    "stale_costing": r"not followed (his|its|their) material|own spreadsheet",
    "partnership_2022": r"kept supplying at the old price",
    "reference_customer": r"important reference customer",
    "approval_2pct": r"above 2 ?% need the approval|pricing committee",
    "deprioritising_us": r"reviewing small accounts|not strategic|reorganising our range"
    r"|supply from stock only|sharpens its focus|focus on customers with volume",
    "price_frozen": r"no room on price|not discounted|price list applies to all|discounts not possible"
    r"|frozen all price reductions",
    "hedged": r"bought (their|our) [\w ,]{1,40} forward|covered at fixed prices|material covered until"
    r"|secures power prices|hedged",
    "complains_late_pay": r"invoices are overdue",
}
# Cost of money per year by owner type (seen in practice: groups 4 to 7 %, family firms 7 to 8.5 %,
# founder-run job shops 12 to 17 %); a cash need adds to it.
RATE = {"group": 0.05, "private": 0.07, "family": 0.075, "founder": 0.12}
DEFAULT_RATE = 0.07


def signals_in(text):
    return sorted(k for k, pat in SIGNALS.items() if re.search(pat, text or "", re.I))


def supplier_texts(pkg, sid):
    """Every text about this supplier: its letters, call and meeting notes and news, from the
    package and the Sunday release (both reach `ids` and `document`), plus its quote remarks."""
    texts = []
    for ref in pkg.ids("doc:") + pkg.ids("news:"):
        row = pkg.lookup(ref) or {}
        if row.get("supplier") != sid and row.get("supplier_id") != sid:
            continue
        try:
            texts.append(pkg.document(ref))
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - a row without a readable file: its headline still counts
            texts.append(" ".join(str(v) for k, v in row.items() if k in ("title", "headline", "body", "subject")))
    try:
        texts += [r.get("remarks") or "" for r in pkg.query("SELECT remarks FROM quotes WHERE supplier_id = ?", (sid,))]
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - no SQLite
        pass
    return texts


"""The live analyst: reads each supplier e-mail as it arrives (the opening quote included) and
tells the bidder the mood of the person writing and the tactic for our next move, so the bidding
follows the supplier we actually meet and not only the one in our files. It also matches the
e-mail to the arguments the demo bidding expected, so the writer gets our prepared answer.
Everything it returns comes from a fixed list; the policy decides what each value changes. Traits
that move anchors or rates stay with the patterns in `personas.py`: a model's guess there costs too
much."""

from . import llm

TIMEOUT_S = 6.0
MOODS = ("warm", "neutral", "irritated", "pressured")
TACTICS = ("steady", "hold", "close_in", "argue")
ASKS = ("volume", "proof", "payment", "target")  # the kinds `policy.asks` reads

SYSTEM = """You are the analyst next to our buyer at Hollerau Pumpenwerke during a negotiation. Read
the supplier's latest e-mail and say who we are dealing with right now and what to do next.
Return JSON only:
{"mood": the mood of the person writing: "warm", "neutral", "irritated" or "pressured",
 "tactic": our best next move, one of:
   "hold" - it still concedes or signals room to move: we move less than usual,
   "close_in" - it says in so many words that this is nearly its last step or that its patience
     is used up: we move further towards its price to keep the talks alive,
   "argue" - it brings an argument we can answer or doubts our data: we answer it with evidence,
   "steady" - none of these,
 "argument": the number of the EXPECTED ARGUMENT its e-mail makes, or 0 if none,
 "asks": what it asks of us, from this list only: volume, proof, payment, target,
 "notes": one or two sentences for the colleague who writes our reply: what this person cares
  about right now and how to answer them. No figures, no dates.}"""


def read(complete, case, body, ours, theirs, arguments=(), timeout=TIMEOUT_S):
    """{mood, tactic, argument, asks, notes} for a supplier e-mail, every value from its list; None
    when the model is off, late or wrong. `ours`, `theirs`: the price paths so far; `arguments`:
    what the demo bidding expected this supplier to say (`argument` indexes them from 1)."""
    expected = "\n".join(f"{i}. {a}" for i, a in enumerate(arguments, 1)) or "none prepared"
    user = (
        f"CASE: {case.get('title')} ({case.get('type')}, goal {case['buyer'].get('category_goal')})\n"
        f"OUR PRICES SO FAR: {ours}\nITS PRICES SO FAR: {theirs}\nEXPECTED ARGUMENTS:\n{expected}\n"
        f"ITS E-MAIL:\n{(body or '')[:2500]}"
    )
    raw = llm.ask_json(complete, SYSTEM, user, min(timeout, TIMEOUT_S))
    if raw is None:
        return None
    asks = raw.get("asks")
    argument = raw.get("argument")
    return {
        "mood": raw.get("mood") if raw.get("mood") in MOODS else "neutral",
        "tactic": raw.get("tactic") if raw.get("tactic") in TACTICS else "steady",
        "argument": argument if isinstance(argument, int) and 0 < argument <= len(arguments) else 0,
        "asks": [a for a in asks if a in ASKS] if isinstance(asks, list) else [],
        "notes": " ".join(str(raw.get("notes") or "").split())[:400],
    }

content.text:
I'd redo the concession controller: `step()` at `buyer/policy.py:861` together with `next_price()` and the patience budgets set in `setup()` (lines 156 to 162). It is the part that decides how far we move each round, and it is the only part where the evidence from the 121 run logs points one way while the code points the other.

**What it does today.** Our move is a fixed share of the gap to the supplier's counter (`FRACTION` 0.3), clipped by a hand-set patience budget per supplier class: 1.0 by default, 0.3 in relationship goals, 0.16 for a fully booked supplier, 0.14 near cost. Below a budget of 0.2 a second rule caps the gap at 1.5 % of its counter. All five numbers were tuned on ten practice suppliers.

**Why it is the weakest piece.** Across the run logs the supplier's concession per round is nearly a schedule of its own and barely responds to the size of our move, as long as we move at all. Kalwisz gives 0.50, 0.50, 0.50 and stops at 45.50 in all 11 runs. Leitner 0.22 then 0.12 in 8 of 8. Donautal 0.05 to 0.10 after round 1. So every cent we move is a cent lost, and every round we stay in earns its next scheduled step. The code does the opposite: it spends 30 % of the gap per round and ends threads after 2 to 4 of the 10 messages allowed.

The same supplier, same anchor, different pacing:

| Case | Our moves after the anchor | Deal | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| P18 e86f45 | 0.20, 0.08, 0.02 | 5.00 | 0.688 |
| P18 436cda | 0.16, 0.08, 0.03 | 5.10 | 0.621 |
| P18 f038c7 | 0.40, 0.17 | 5.50 | 0.431 |
| P08 0e897a | 0.19, 0.11, 0.07 | 5.24 | 0.670 |
| P08 5d30fb | 0.46, 0.19, 0.01 | 5.42 | 0.471 |
| P05 Dralveck 50df27 | 0.06 | 27.92 | 0.822 |
| P05 Dralveck fbb9b6 | 2.32 | 30.18 | 0.588 |

The clearest single loss is P10, 7 of 7 runs identical. The `capacity_full` signal sets the budget to 0.16, the 1.5 % cap fires in round 2, and we jump from 29.95 to 31.22 after Ravensteiner moved 0.50. It agrees at 31.50 at once. C_best decodes to 28.21 at 42 days, so that one rule left about 190k EUR, a tenth of C, on the table every time. Learnings already records the same thing from the other side: "40 % move = 30 % move", "a slow walk of 12 % per round got five counters and 5.31 against four and 5.33 to 5.39", and the first open question is "moves sized to the supplier's observed cap instead of a share of the gap".

**Why this is the generalisation risk, not just a tuning issue.** The budgets branch on a signal and a goal and then apply a constant learned from one or two suppliers. A new supplier in the final that carries `capacity_full` text gets Hrvelec's patience number whether or not it behaves like Hrvelec. The anchor table has the same shape but the evidence says anchors barely move the first counter, so the loss there is small. The pacing is where the constants bite.

**What I would build instead.** A reciprocal controller that reads the thread instead of the class:

- Size our move from the supplier's last concession, roughly matching it, with a floor at the smallest move that has kept this supplier moving and a ceiling that never exceeds its own step. A generous bot gets more, a stingy one gets 0.50 for its 0.50, never 1.27.
- Spend the message budget. Plan to use the rounds left, not to be within a fixed share of its price by round 3. Close in only when its concession shrinks toward zero two rounds running, or it says final, or messages run out. The analyst's `close_in` tactic already exists as a hook.
- Keep the cumulative-gap guard as a safety ceiling only, set from the walk-aways actually observed, Nordmark at 19 % and Dralveck at 39 %, rather than as the pacing device. Keep `MIN_MOVE`, the no-repeat guard and the deep-floor hold, which the data supports.

The thing that stays is what the data does support: suppliers answer a moving sheet with their next scheduled step, and they call final when we stop moving or sit too far away for too long. A controller built on those two observed facts transfers to a supplier we have never seen. Five constants tuned to ten suppliers do not.

**Caveat.** This is in-sample. The free check is to replay the recorded paths on the simulator and a sandbox foundry, then spend practice quota only on P08, P18 and P10, where the spread between runs is largest and the floor is known from C_best.

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

entries.name: EnterWorktree
entries.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

name.description: Optional name for a new worktree. Each "/"-separated segment may contain only letters, digits, dots, underscores, and dashes; max 64 chars total. A random name is generated if not provided. Mutually exclusive with `path`.

path.description: Path to an existing worktree to switch into instead of creating a new one. Must appear in `git worktree list` for the current repo — or, on first entry from the launch directory, for a repo nested inside it (multi-repo workspace). Mutually exclusive with `name`.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.
